items.markdown:

### What to Look For / Ask Before Signing:

1. **No Win, No Fee Structure:** Ensure you understand what costs are covered. While legal fees are usually deferred until you win, check whether **disbursements** (such as independent medical reports or court fees) must be paid upfront or if they are strictly deferred.[[1]](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/superannuation-and-insurance/total-and-permanent-disability-tpd-claims)[[2]](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/superannuation-and-insurance)
2. **Specialist Focus:** Make sure the lawyer specifically handles *superannuation insurance law* , not just general motor vehicle or WorkCover injury law, as TPD relies strictly on contract/policy definitions and medical proof of work incapacity.[[1]](https://www.mauriceblackburn.com.au/injury-illness/superannuation-insurance-claims/total-permanent-disability-melbourne/)[[2]](https://www.lhd.com.au/office-location/vic/melbourne/tpd-superannuation-claims/)
3. **Free Claim Review:** Most of these top-tier firms offer a free initial assessment to tell you whether your policy was active on your last day worked and if your medical evidence meets the definition of TPD.[[1]](https://www.shine.com.au/service/super-and-disability-insurance)[[2]](https://www.mauriceblackburn.com.au/injury-illness/superannuation-insurance-claims/total-permanent-disability-melbourne/)

To help me narrow down which firm might best suit your situation, could you tell me:

- What is the **nature of the injury or illness** (physical, psychological, or chronic)?
- Are you looking for a firm to **start a fresh claim** or to **appeal a rejected claim**?
